capabilities.name: banner_and_softversion_parse
capabilities.description: Parse the SSH identification string (SSH-<protoversion>-<softwareversion> <comments>) for softwareversion/product+version and the trailing comment tag (Ubuntu/Debian/FreeBSD build suffix) that CPE-maps to distro + patch level.
capabilities.notes: svcdetect.py already regex-matches SSH-2.0-OpenSSH_/dropbear/libssh/ROSSSH; a dedicated module should also capture the free-form comment (e.g. 'Ubuntu-3ubuntu0.10') for CVE/patch-level pinning and feed the distro back to Host.os.

capabilities.name: legacy_protocol_version
capabilities.description: Flag servers advertising SSH-1.99 (dual-stack) or SSH-1.x, which allow the trivially broken SSH-1 transport (CRC-32 compensation attack, no MAC).

capabilities.name: algorithm_kexinit_enum
capabilities.description: Send our own SSH_MSG_KEXINIT and read the server's KEXINIT to enumerate all offered kex_algorithms, server_host_key_algorithms, encryption/mac/compression algorithms (client_to_server and server_to_server) and the languages/first_kex_packet_follows flags.
capabilities.notes: This is the foundation probe — every posture finding below reads from the KEXINIT lists it captures.

capabilities.name: weak_kex_algorithms
capabilities.description: Flag offered kex methods that are cryptographically deprecated: diffie-hellman-group1-sha1 (1024-bit MODP), diffie-hellman-group14-sha1, diffie-hellman-group-exchange-sha1, and any rsa1024-*.

capabilities.name: weak_cipher_mac_suites
capabilities.description: Flag offered ciphers/MACs that are broken or discouraged: arcfour/arcfour128/arcfour256, 3des-cbc, blowfish-cbc, cast128-cbc, any *-cbc (plaintext-recovery), hmac-md5*, hmac-sha1-96, umac-64, or the null cipher/'none' MAC.

capabilities.name: hostkey_algorithm_posture
capabilities.description: Grade the offered server_host_key_algorithms list — ssh-rsa (SHA-1 signature) deprecated (OpenSSH 8.7+ disables by default), ssh-dss/1024-bit DSA broken, prefer rsa-sha2-256/512 and ssh-ed25519.

capabilities.name: hostkey_fingerprint_capture
capabilities.description: Complete the DH/ECDH key exchange to the point of reading SSH_MSG_KEX_ECDH_REPLY (or SSH_MSG_KEXDH_REPLY / GEX_REPLY) and extract the K_S host key blob; compute MD5-colon-hex and SHA256-base64 fingerprints matching ssh-keygen -l output.
capabilities.notes: Fingerprints are the primary correlator for host-cloning and cross-network SSH-pivot detection — justifies a NEW known_hostkeys shared surface.

capabilities.name: auth_methods_enum
capabilities.description: Send SSH_MSG_USERAUTH_REQUEST with method 'none' for a benign username after SSH_MSG_SERVICE_ACCEPT of ssh-userauth; the server replies SSH_MSG_USERAUTH_FAILURE carrying the comma-list of methods that can continue (password, publickey, keyboard-interactive, gssapi-with-mic, hostbased).

capabilities.name: password_auth_permitted
capabilities.description: If auth_methods_enum returns 'password' or 'keyboard-interactive', flag interactive password auth exposed to the network — spraying and brute-force become viable and the server cannot enforce MFA at the transport layer.
capabilities.protocol_reference: RFC 4252 §8 (Password Authentication) / RFC 4256 (Generic Message Exchange Auth)

capabilities.name: root_login_probe
capabilities.description: Send a userauth 'none' for user 'root'; if the failure list is empty or the server responds SSH_MSG_USERAUTH_SUCCESS to a subsequent publickey-hasSig=false probe, PermitRootLogin is enabled — target for spray + key-in-loot re-use.

capabilities.name: username_enum_cve_2016_6210
capabilities.description: Timing-differential on SHA-512 crypt() when a long invalid password is sent for a valid vs invalid user — valid users take measurably longer on OpenSSH < 7.3; probe with a bounded set of names and record latency.

capabilities.name: username_enum_pkt_size_cve_2018_15473
capabilities.description: Send a malformed SSH_MSG_USERAUTH_REQUEST publickey packet; OpenSSH < 7.7 responds differently (immediate failure vs disconnect) for valid vs invalid usernames — enumerates users pre-auth.

capabilities.name: pubkey_hassig_false_probe
capabilities.description: For each collected private/public key in loot and each known_user, send SSH_MSG_USERAUTH_REQUEST publickey with has_signature=FALSE; a PK_OK reply proves the key is authorized (no crypto op, no logged login) — turns a stolen public key into a confirmed access finding.

capabilities.name: terrapin_cve_2023_48795
capabilities.description: Flag KEXINIT that offers ChaCha20-Poly1305@openssh.com or any CBC cipher with *-etm@openssh.com MAC AND does NOT advertise kex-strict-s-v00@openssh.com / kex-strict-c-v00@openssh.com in kex_algorithms — the Terrapin prefix-truncation attack is applicable.

capabilities.name: known_backdoored_builds
capabilities.description: Match softwareversion against a small curated map of trojaned/backdoored SSH distributions (Dropbear 2016.72 supply-chain, xz-utils sshd backdoor CVE-2024-3094 via liblzma link, OpenSSH regreSSHion CVE-2024-6387 for 8.5p1–9.7p1 on glibc).

capabilities.name: hostkey_reuse_correlation
capabilities.description: Group all discovered SSH hosts by SHA256 host-key fingerprint; identical keys across distinct IPs prove a golden-image / NAT / same-appliance relationship (or a stolen host-key) worth pivoting on.
capabilities.notes: Consumes the proposed known_hostkeys surface — also feeds the attack-path graph as an implicit trust edge.

cross_service_wire_candidates: known_hostnames: the SSH banner comment often carries distro build tags ('Ubuntu-3ubuntu0.10', 'FreeBSD-20240101') and, on some appliances, the hostname — feed distro into Host.os and any hostname tokens into known_hostnames
known_users: valid usernames confirmed by CVE-2016-6210 timing or CVE-2018-15473 packet-size oracle become high-confidence entries in known_users (Linux realm, source='ssh_userenum')
known_users: usernames the auth 'none' probe implicitly validates when root_login_probe or a specific user gets a distinct methods-continue list

known_hashes: a captured hostkey (K_S blob) is not a crackable hash, but a SHA256:base64 fingerprint is the right key for a NEW shared surface 'known_hostkeys' — lets ssh, rdp (NLA/ECDSA), sftp and jump-host detection share one identity per box

relay_targets: an SSH endpoint where publickey with a loot-key returned PK_OK is a confirmed pivot target — emit relay_targets with method='ssh-pubkey' and the accepted key id so the pivot planner can use it directly
relay_targets: any host advertising password auth for a known_users entry is a spray-relay candidate

NEW surface 'known_hostkeys' proposed: {fingerprint_sha256, key_type, seen_on:[ip:port], first_source} — correlates SSH across the estate, detects golden-image clones, and is a natural place to record ssh-keyscan output from credentialed sessions

recce/services/serviceenum.py (name 'ssh' -> script 'ssh' at line 12; port 22 -> 'ssh' at line 38)

existing_coverage.notes: Detection + a version-parse + nmap NSE run is all recce currently has for SSH. There is NO dedicated recce/services/ssh.py, no in-process KEXINIT parser, no hostkey capture into models, no auth-methods enum in Python (only whatever the nmap NSE returned), and no findings module wiring SSH posture into the vuln totals the way ftp/smtp/vnc do.

implementation_notes: Build recce/services/ssh.py modelled on services/ftp.py (banner+probe+findings shape) but with a small binary framer since SSH is packetised, not line-based. Read the identification string until CRLF (RFC 4253 §4.2 — up to 255 bytes, may be preceded by other lines), then send our own identification string 'SSH-2.0-recce_<ver>\\r\\n', then send SSH_MSG_KEXINIT and read the server's KEXINIT — that alone unlocks the algo-inventory + weak-kex/cipher/mac + hostkey-posture + Terrapin findings without doing DH. Hostkey fingerprint requires one more round (SSH_MSG_KEXDH_INIT / KEX_ECDH_INIT with e = g^x mod p or curve25519-donna) — the stdlib doesn't ship curve25519, so either use cryptography (already a recce dependency?) or implement a Curve25519 X25519 in pure Python (~40 lines) to stay airgap-clean. Auth-methods enum is one more round after NEWKEYS/service-request but requires the derived keys — easiest path is to shell out to `ssh -o PreferredAuthentications=none -o BatchMode=yes` and parse stderr (matches recce's shell-out-to-Kali-tooling pattern in deploy.py), OR use paramiko if allowed. Recommend the pure-socket path for KEXINIT/hostkey (deterministic + airgap-safe) and shell-out to `ssh` for the userauth probes (matches existing style). Reuse svccommon.finding_builder and svcprobe.iter_probe like ftp.py does. Reuse svcdetect._PRODUCT_RE for banner parsing — don't duplicate. Emit a new known_hostkeys shared surface under recce/core/ mirroring known_hostnames.py shape.

recommended_findings.title: SSH-1 or SSH-1.99 legacy protocol enabled
SSH host key algorithm ssh-rsa (SHA-1) offered
SSH host key algorithm ssh-dss (1024-bit DSA) offered
SSH weak key exchange offered (dh-group1-sha1 / gex-sha1)
SSH vulnerable to Terrapin prefix truncation (CVE-2023-48795)
SSH root login permitted (auth methods reachable for root)
SSH username enumeration via packet-size oracle (CVE-2018-15473)
SSH publickey from loot accepted (PK_OK to hasSig=false) — confirmed access
SSH host key reused across multiple hosts (golden image / clone)
SSH banner leaks OS distribution + patch tag

summary: SSH (RFC 4253 transport, RFC 4252 authentication) is a packetised binary protocol whose opening moves — the CRLF identification string and the SSH_MSG_KEXINIT exchange — leak everything an attacker needs to grade the server's cryptographic posture before any credential is spent: the full server-offered kex/hostkey/cipher/MAC/compression lists, the softwareversion (OpenSSH/dropbear/libssh/ROSSSH plus a distro comment tag), and after one more round the host key itself. What an attacker actually wants from SSH is (a) fingerprints of the host key for cross-network correlation and MITM baselines, (b) a graded posture (ssh-rsa deprecated, ssh-dss broken, *-cbc & hmac-md5 weak, Terrapin exposure via ChaCha20/EtM-CBC without kex-strict), (c) the concrete authentication methods the server will accept for a given username (via the RFC 4252 §5.2 'none' request) and whether root is reachable, and (d) a low-cost way to turn any collected private key into a confirmed foothold using SSH_MSG_USERAUTH_REQUEST publickey with hasSig=false (a PK_OK reply proves acceptance without a login event). Recce today detects the port and mines the banner, but has no dedicated ssh module — the whole KEXINIT/hostkey/auth-methods loop is delegated to nmap NSE and never lands in models. A recce/services/ssh.py modelled on services/ftp.py would ship this, feed the OS field, and emit a new known_hostkeys shared surface so SSH identity is correlatable across the estate.
